source_title: China's EdTech Works Until Authority Has To Survive Online
summary: This April 25, 2020 T4 Education interview turns China's emergency online schooling into an education stress test: infrastructure can deliver information, but it cannot automatically reproduce peer comparison, exam ritual, teacher authority, or classroom control.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Chinese schooling is built around extrinsic motivation, peer comparison, rewards, praise, and self-worth rather than information delivery alone.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The interview gives an early COVID-era instance of the school-game mechanism: the student's behavior is formed by the rewarded game around parents, teachers, peers, tests, and status, not by learning content alone.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The Gaokao delay and classroom peer-comparison material show how much trust and motivational pressure Chinese families place in the visible exam system.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The source does not repeat the later institutional-trust argument directly, but it gives a dated stress signal: postponing the Gaokao is treated as extraordinary because the exam is the central social and motivational object.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Add online schooling as a stress test of the education soul game: when school is treated as information delivery, edtech can look successful; when the hidden machinery is peer comparison, pep-rally intensity, parental support, and teacher authority, moving online exposes what the classroom had been holding together.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Education owns the mechanism because the active pressure is how the school game forms motivation and authority. Platform Infrastructure owns app-store and online-medium mechanics only if later sources center the platform layer itself.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the teacher-authority reversal as a vivid example: teachers are treated like gods in the physical classroom, but online the students know the medium better and can downvote apps, report pirated software, or weaponize homonyms against the teacher.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: The example belongs in Education because Jiang explains the sabotage as resentment produced by teacher control. Attention or Platform concepts would own it only when the emphasis shifts from school authority to platform capture or algorithmic infrastructure.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Mention only as contrast if a later living-school pass compares dead information delivery with a school that trains judgment: this source shows why content transfer is not enough to preserve a living educational form.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Keep the main extension in Education. Living School owns future-making education, not every COVID online-schooling diagnosis.

new_lens_seeds.title: Medium Flips Classroom Authority
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: An institution can preserve formal authority in one medium while losing practical control in another; when students understand the new medium better than the teacher, latent resentment becomes usable sabotage.
new_lens_seeds.why_reusable: The mechanism applies beyond this short interview whenever a hierarchy moves online and discovers that authority depended on physical setting, ritual, surveillance, peer pressure, or adult technical superiority that the new medium removes.

chronology_notes.note: On 2020-04-25, Jiang treats the Gaokao postponement as live evidence from the first COVID shock, not as retrospective pandemic analysis; this makes the source an early dated stress test for Education As A Soul Game.
This source precedes the July 22, 2020 learning-journal interview: April gives the negative online-authority stress test, while July gives Jiang's positive meta-learning response to COVID disruption.
